studies.Title: Intake of fiber and fiber-rich plant foods is associated with a lower risk of renal cell carcinoma in a large US cohort.
studies.Reference: Intake of fiber and fiber-rich plant foods is associated with a lower risk of renal cell carcinoma in a large US cohort.
studies.Journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
studies.Population: NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study participants
studies.comparison_type: Highest versus lowest quintile of legume intake

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Design: Participants of the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study ( n = 491,841) completed a self-administered questionnaire of demographics, diet, lifestyle, and medical history. Over 9 (mean) years of follow-up we identified 1816 incident cases of RCC.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: Over 9 (mean) years of follow-up we identified 1816 incident cases of RCC.
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: Intakes of legumes, whole grains, and cruciferous vegetables were also associated with a 16–18% reduced risk of RCC.
extraction_supporting_text.design: In a large prospective cohort of US men and women, we comprehensively investigated dietary intake and food sources of fiber in relation to RCC risk.
extraction_supporting_text.timing: Over 9 (mean) years of follow-up we identified 1816 incident cases of RCC.
extraction_supporting_text.continent: In a large prospective cohort of US men and women
extraction_supporting_text.gender: In a large prospective cohort of US men and women
extraction_supporting_text.smoking_status: The inverse association between fiber intake and RCC was consistent among participants who never smoked
